devices.title: IKEA E1744
devices.notes:
If you want to use the default controller, you will need to set `legacy: false` in the Zigbee2MQTT configuration.
Read more [here](https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/devices/E1744.html#legacy-integration).

devices.title: IKEA E1810
devices.notes: This device mapping also supports the E1524 controller.

devices.title: IKEA E2002
devices.notes:
This controller fires the "on" action when the arrows are held, as well as the hold arrow action.
This means that when long pressing the arrows, the light(s) will turn on before changing the color.

This device mapping also supports the E2001 controller.

devices.title: IKEA E2123
devices.notes:
The device supports other events which are not added to the default mapping. Please check
[this GitHub issue](https://github.com/xaviml/controllerx/issues/842) for more information.

devices.title: Philips HueDimmer
devices.notes:
When using **z2m**, the device needs to be flagged as `legacy: false`, as the
[Zigbee2MQTT documentation recommends](https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/devices/324131092621.html#options).

When using **z2m** and the multiple clicks functionality, make sure to remove the
`multiple_press_timeout` option from the device-specific configuration (`devices.yaml`).

When using **deCONZ**, all the click actions are mapped to the X002 actions, which are fired
when the button is released after being clicked.

devices.title: Lutron PJ22B
devices.notes:
For the State integration, it requires the [LutronCasetaPro](https://github.com/upsert/lutron-caseta-pro)
**custom** integration by upsert. **This will not work with the default Lutron Caseta integration.**
All Lutron Caseta Pro Pico remotes supported by LutronCasetaPro are supported using this
controller type, except for the 4-button PJ2-4B remotes, which have their own controller.

devices.title: Aqara MFKZQ01LM
devices.notes:
This controller does not have a self-explanatory way to be used, since its main
purpose is to be customized. This is why we recommend customizing it with a
[custom mapping](../advanced/index.md).

The deCONZ integration should be added with [type gesture](../start/integrations/deconz.md).

devices.title: Müller Licht MLI404011
devices.notes:
Some buttons are not mapped yet for either integration.
Read more about it [here (deCONZ)](https://github.com/xaviml/controllerx/issues/111)
and [here (z2m)](https://github.com/xaviml/controllerx/issues/176).

devices.title: Namron 4512773
devices.notes:
The Namron 4512773 has four groups, and with swappable physical buttons it is intended to control one, two, or four buttons.
To make this work with ControllerX, you can use one app per light you want to control.

devices.title: OSRAM AC025XX00NJ
devices.notes:
This controller is supported for AC0251100NJ / AC0251400NJ / AC0251600NJ / AC0251700NJ.
The different models are just different colours.

devices.title: Philips 929003017102
devices.notes:
This controller has 4 modes, and depending on which one is used,
it will trigger one action or another: single_rocker, single_push_button, dual_rocker, dual_push_button.
You can read more about it in these threads:
[deCONZ](https://github.com/dresden-elektronik/deconz-rest-plugin/issues/4566) and
[Zigbee2MQTT](https://github.com/Koenkk/zigbee-herdsman-converters/issues/2393).

devices.title: Philips PTM215X
devices.notes: Check the button mapping [here](https://phoscon.de/en/support#pairing-friends-of-hue-switch).

devices.title: ROBB ROB2000070
devices.notes:
Note that each button performs the same actions.
This is because ControllerX is designed to control just one entity (light or media player).
So, you can include the `actions` parameter to include the actions needed,
or use the `mapping` attribute to define a [custom mapping](../advanced/index.md).
You can check [here](https://github.com/xaviml/controllerx/issues/18#issuecomment-582535634) for reference.

This controller is a white-label version of the Sunricher SR-ZG9001K8-DIM.

devices.title: Tuya TS0044
devices.notes:
Note that each button performs the same actions.
This is because ControllerX is designed to control just one entity (light or media player).
So, you can include the `actions` parameter to include the actions needed,
or use the `mapping` attribute to define a [custom mapping](../advanced/index.md).
You can check [here](https://github.com/xaviml/controllerx/issues/18#issuecomment-582535634) for reference.

Also, this controller supports the hold action, but not release. This means that there are no
smooth brightness changes when holding, just step by step every time it is held.

devices.title: Tuya TS0044F
devices.notes:
This device is very similar to the TS0044 Tuya, except that it doesn't support hold actions or double clicks.

Note that each button performs the same actions.
This is because ControllerX is designed to control just one entity (light or media player).
So, you can include the `actions` parameter to include the actions needed,
or use the `mapping` attribute to define a [custom mapping](../advanced/index.md).
You can check [here](https://github.com/xaviml/controllerx/issues/18#issuecomment-582535634) for reference.

Since this controller doesn't support the hold action, there are no smooth brightness
changes, just step by step every time it is pressed.
